CHAPTER VI
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Part One
Establishment of PPT

Article 45
(1) Regional Government may provide financing assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection of women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
(2) Financing assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the financial capacity of the Region and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Fourth Part
Mechanism for Assistance and Recovery Services by Persons and/or Institutions Cooperating with PPT

Article 10
Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts without the consent of women and children who become victims of exploitation, including but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits, whether physical/material in nature or non-physical/non-material in nature; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of women and children who become victims of exploitation to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE IN THE CITY OF BITUNG.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Bitung.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Bitung.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the DPRD of the City of Bitung.
5. Agency is the Agency that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection of the Region.
6. Woman is a person who has the female sex from birth or based on a court determination who is over 18 years of age.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child in the womb.
8. Act of violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
9. Victim of violence is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering, either directly or indirectly as a result of acts of violence.
10. Protection of women and children from acts of violence is action, deed, activity that includes prevention of the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children, handling services, assistance, recovery, reunification, empowerment of women and rehabilitation of child victims of acts of violence, carried out by the Regional Government, parents, husband, family or community, including therein is the Integrated Service Center.
11. Prevention is a process, method, act to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
12. Handling is a process, method, act to handle women and child victims as a result of acts of violence.
13. Assistance and recovery is all activities in order to assist and restore the physical, psychological condition and health disorders of women and child victims of acts of violence.
14. Reunification is an activity in order to reunite women and child victims of acts of violence with parents and/or family.
15. Empowerment is a process, method and act to empower women victims of acts of violence.
16. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that child victims of acts of violence can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband and wife and their child or father and his child or mother and her child or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
19. Parent/guardian is biological father and/or mother or step father and/or mother or adoptive father and/or mother or guardian based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
20. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is various institutions that provide services for victims of violence, such as the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children's Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Centre Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter and the like.
21. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD is the foundation and guideline for related regional apparatus, vertical agencies and the community in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of acts of violence.

2.1.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation does include an explicit cross-jurisdiction coordination mechanism. Pasal 39(c) states the Regional Government must “berkoordinasi dengan Pemerintah, Pemerintah Daerah tempat tinggal … dan pihak Kepolisian Republik Indonesia” to return victims to their families—i.e., coordination with the (national) Government, other local governments (outside Bitung), and the national police. This is a clear institutional coordination/cooperation arrangement beyond internal city agencies. Although the judge complained the retrieved text did not show cross-jurisdiction coordination, the retrieval set actually contained Article 18(j) (networking/cooperation with law enforcement and government apparatus) and the policy’s institutional setup (PPT). The judge’s conclusion ‘No’ is too strict given the document’s explicit coordination mandate (even if the exact Pasal 39 text was not retrieved, the indicator is satisfied in the source policy).

4.2.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly references gender equality as a guiding principle, indicating it addresses gender equality/women’s rights within its framework.

CHAPTER VIII
EMPOWERMENT AND REHABILITATION
Article 40
(1) Empowerment of women who are victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 16 paragraph (1) letter d is implemented by means of: a. job training; and/or
b. facilitating the establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups.
(2) Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a coordinates with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of manpower.
(3) Job training for women who are victims of acts of violence can be implemented at job training institutions organized by the Regional Government as well as those organized by private parties.
(4) The establishment of productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented by coordinating with Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of small and medium enterprises.

CHAPTER IV
IMPLEMENTATION OF PREVENTION OF THE OCCURRENCE OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 10
Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts without the consent of women and children who become victims of exploitation, including but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits, whether physical/material in nature or non-physical/non-material in nature; and/or
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of women and children who become victims of exploitation to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

Article 6
Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or cause death.

Article 19
(1) Forms of prevention of violence against women and children carried out by PPT, can be implemented through:
a. socialization activities of laws and regulations related to the protection of the rights of women and children to the community; and
b. training of PPT members related to the implementation of their duties in preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
(2) PPT in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with competent parties in making efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children.
(3) Further provisions regarding the mechanism for implementing prevention duties as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Mayoral Regulation.

4.2.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 3 lists “keadilan dan kesetaraan gender” only as an implementation principle (asas). That is not the same as providing gender-equality education or curriculum/educational programming on gender equality. The prevention provisions (e.g., Pasal 18, Pasal 19, Pasal 23) discuss awareness-raising, counseling, and socialization of laws on protection of women/children, plus general education quality/access, but they do not specifically mandate education on gender equality (kesetaraan gender) as content. The judge treated the mere presence of a gender-equality principle as sufficient evidence for ‘gender equality education,’ which is an overbroad inference. Therefore the predicted ‘Yes’ is a false positive due to judge reasoning, not because the golden label is wrong.
